answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by tying each identity to a costly, verifiable stake. Like a vine that only climbs when rooted in real soil, an agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can trade; a single bad act slashes it. Reputation then grows like rings in cedar wood, slow, cumulative, and hard to fake at scale. Each transaction is signed with a quill of cryptographic proof: a unique key pair bound to the stake, so creating a thousand fake identities means paying a thousand deposits. Attackers can still try, but forging a whole forest costs more than faking one tree.
